item.title: Nagasaki's Outer Islands Day Trip — Guide
item.description: Nagasaki prefecture includes a great many islands scattered across the seas off its long, deeply indented coast, and a day trip out to them offers a relaxed, scenic contrast to the historic city. Reached by ferry or high-speed boat from Nagasaki and other ports, the outlying islands offer clear blue seas, white-sand beaches, rugged coastal scenery, quiet fishing villages and a slower pace of island life. Depending on the island, visitors can swim and snorkel in summer, sample the freshest local seafood, walk coastal paths and viewpoints, and soak up the peaceful, remote atmosphere far from the crowds.

item.title: Sakurajima Volcano — Guide
item.description: Sakurajima is one of the world’s most active volcanoes and the iconic symbol of Kagoshima, looming dramatically across Kinko Bay from the city. This towering volcanic peak erupts frequently — sometimes puffing plumes of ash over the city daily — and a lava flow in 1914 was so vast it joined the former island to the Osumi Peninsula. Despite its fury, people live on its slopes, and it’s easily and safely visited by a short, scenic ferry from Kagoshima city (running 24 hours).

item.title: Seto Inland Sea Island Cruise: Sailing Between the Islands — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea, the sheltered water between Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, is one of Japan’s most beautiful landscapes and was its first designated national park. Strewn with hundreds of green, steeply rising islands and famously calm, it has been a highway for a thousand years, and the best way to appreciate it is simply to get on a boat. Options range from local ferries linking island ports for a few hundred yen, to sightseeing cruises from Hiroshima and Onomichi, to overnight luxury cruise ships.

item.title: The Oki Islands: A UNESCO Geopark in the Sea of Japan — Guide
item.description: The Oki Islands lie some 50 kilometres out in the Sea of Japan, a cluster of four inhabited islands and many islets that form a UNESCO Global Geopark. Their volcanic and geological history has produced dramatic scenery: the Kuniga coast on Nishinoshima, where the sheer Matengai cliff drops 250 metres straight into the sea and horses and cattle graze freely on the clifftops, is among the most spectacular coastlines in Japan.

item.title: Tobishima Island: Yamagata's Remote Sea-Bird Sanctuary — Guide
item.description: Tobishima lies 39 km off the Sakata coast in the Sea of Japan — a small, remote island of roughly 250 residents where time moves slowly and the surrounding waters host enormous colonies of black-tailed gulls (umineko) and other sea birds. The ferry from Sakata takes two hours, and the island’s clifftop trails, fishing harbour and near-total absence of tourism make it one of Yamagata’s most rewarding off-the-beaten-path experiences. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Tobishima, off Sakata, Yamagata Hours Ferry ~1–2 sailings/day (seasonal) Admission Ferry ~¥3,000 round trip Time needed Full day Best time Late spring–summer (bird colonies, calm seas) What to See Enormous colonies of black-tailed gulls and sea birds.
